session: in-car, DSP USB connected, ~10 min window, reads only (no writes)
finding: Crossover (cmd 13 / PassBand) is READABLE without a new command: the existing /api/eqread uses ReadSubCmd.EqAndPassBand and the reply is the full StructEqAndPassBand (1044 bytes) - the passband was already on the wire, just not decoded.

decode.method: eqread wireHex: payload = wire[8 .. len-4]; passband scalars at payload+872; LE

vendor_evidence.per_filter_state: each mHlps[n] carries Fc, hiLowType, Slope, filterType, butt_Type, Enable (AP.cs:1918-1943) - hiLowType is NOT transmitted on the wire (cmd 13 struct has no such field)

unknowns: Filter roles: wire struct names slots 'low*/high*' but vendor state stores hiLowType per filter which does NOT go on the wire - which slot is the HPF vs LPF for a given path is not proven from this data alone
Slope code table (1/2/3 -> dB/oct) and type code (1 -> Butterworth vs Linkwitz-Riley) not confirmed against vendor UI
resolved_after_user_input: User (in car, 2026-10-16): subs are NOT on any DSP output - they run on a totally separate amplifier. So no path showing a sub-like band is CORRECT, not a decode bug; all 8 DSP outputs are non-sub bands (110..20000). Closes the long-open 'which channels play subs' question: none of them. Implications: DSP EQ/crossover/master never touches the subs; RTA still measures them IF the sub amp is fed stimulus from the head unit (its signal source not yet documented).
safety: all 8 reads via existing eqread API; zero cmd-13 writes; device state untouched
